blocks.text: Joints can be subject to a variety of injuries, which can result in pain, swelling, and reduced motion. Here are some common injuries to joints:

A dislocation is when the bones in a joint are forced out of their normal positions. This can happen as a result of a sudden impact or trauma. A severe dislocation can cause tearing of the muscles, ligaments and tendons. Symptoms include swelling, intense pain, and immobility of the affected joint. Rheumatoid arthritis can also cause joint dislocation. A dislocated joint can only be successfully corrected by a physiotherapist. Surgery may be needed to repair or tighten the stretched ligaments.
book_errors: A dislocated joint can only be successfully corrected by a physiotherapist.

blocks.alt: Two rows. Normal elbow joint: a circle shows the humerus end fitting into the notch of the ulna with the radius beside it, next to a bent arm. Dislocated elbow joint: the ulna and radius are pushed back off the end of the humerus, and the arm beside it bulges at the back of the elbow. Labels: Humerus, Radius, Ulna.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.16: Dislocation in elbow joint (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.16).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: A dislocated joint is put back in place (reduced) by a doctor; it is a medical procedure, often done after an X-ray and with pain relief. Physiotherapy helps the joint recover afterwards.

A sprain is an injury to the ligaments that connect bones in a joint. Commonly injured ligaments are in the ankle, knee and wrist. This can happen when the joint is forced beyond its normal range of motion, causing the ligaments to stretch or tear. Sprains are usually treated with physical therapy. Dressings is done to immobilize the sprain and provide support.

blocks.alt: Two rows. Foot turned inward: a lower leg with the foot rolled inward (arrow), and beside it the ankle bones seen from the outer side with the outer ligament torn. Foot turned outward: the foot rolled outward, and the ankle bones seen from the inner side with the inner ligament torn.
